crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Personalised Wealth Advice
children.blurb: Personalised wealth advice is the practice of shaping a portfolio around one household's goals, tax position, time horizon, liquidity needs and tolerance for loss.

children.name: Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance
children.blurb: Portfolio optimisation beyond mean and variance covers methods that treat risk as more than the standard deviation of returns.

children.name: Tail Risk Hedging
children.blurb: Tail risk hedging in portfolio construction covers the deliberate use of instruments and overlays to limit losses from rare, severe market moves, such as crashes, volatility spikes, or correlation breakdowns.

children.name: Sustainability Factors in Portfolios
children.blurb: Sustainability factors in portfolios are the environmental, social and governance characteristics of holdings that investors use alongside financial measures.

children.name: Pricing Illiquid Assets
children.blurb: Pricing illiquid assets covers the valuation of holdings that do not trade on a public market, such as private equity, private credit, real estate, infrastructure, and stakes in private companies.

sections.body: Portfolio construction is the work of deciding what a person or institution should hold, in what amounts, and why, and then keeping those holdings in line with the reason. Artificial intelligence is now used across that work in concrete ways: models read filings and market data to estimate risk, optimisers search across thousands of candidate weights under constraints, and language models turn a client's stated goals into something a system can act on. The site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, and those prices feed the same kinds of estimation and backtesting pipelines that any portfolio desk uses. The aim is not a machine that picks winners but a set of tools that make the trade-offs visible and repeatable.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The parts that are solved are mostly mechanical. Mean and variance optimisation is well understood, and so is the plumbing that turns a target allocation into orders. What is not solved is the part that matters most: knowing whether a model's estimate of future risk is right, and knowing when a client's circumstances have changed enough that the old plan no longer fits. Tail risk is where the honest limits show, because rare events are by definition rare in the data, and a model trained on a calm decade has little to say about a violent month. Sustainability factors add a second problem, since the underlying measures are inconsistent across providers and often rest on disclosure that is voluntary. Illiquid assets resist pricing altogether, and any number attached to them is an estimate with a wide band around it. Nothing here is advice, and none of these methods removes the need for judgement.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages divide the field by the kind of decision being made. Personalised Wealth Advice is the entry point, covering how goals, time horizons and constraints get translated into a plan a system can work with. Portfolio Optimisation Beyond Mean and Variance goes a level deeper into the mathematics, for readers who want to know what changes when you stop assuming returns are normal. Tail Risk Hedging sits beside it and deals with the extreme end of the distribution, the losses that ordinary variance measures understate. Sustainability Factors in Portfolios handles the non-financial objectives that increasingly appear in mandates, and the measurement problems that come with them. Pricing Illiquid Assets closes the set by asking how to value what does not trade, which is often the hardest number in the whole exercise. A reader new to the area should start with the first page, while someone already comfortable with optimisation will find the middle three most useful together.
